div.head: RUNCORN SCHOOL BOARD.
div.p: RUNCORN SCHOOL BOARD.

The monthly meeting was held on Wednesday morning. The Rev. Canon Barclay presided, and there were also present the Rev. William Fennelly, and Messrs. Simpson, Norman, Pritchard, Lea, Briscoe, and Rigby (clerk).

div.head: ALTERATIONS AT MILL B ROW SCHOOL.
div.p: THE ALTERATIONS AT MILL B ROW SCHOOL.

The Rev. W. FENNELLY made some remarks, in reply to a question from the Chairman, as to the proposed alterations at Mill Brow schooll with the object of giving accommoda- tion for about SO additional scholars. A specification for the work was laid before the Board by Mr. Caygill, builder and joiner, Church-street, the total cost being put at £lB 10s. After some discussion the Rev. W. FENNELLY proposed that the scheme as reported upon should be adopted ; that the plan of Mr. Caygiti be accepted, he to produce a speci- fication to the satisfaction a the committee; as well as an undertaking to carry out the work according to his agree- ment and to their satistaction. Mr. NORMAN seconded the proposition. Mr. Stiwpsolt : Are we quite sure that as we have had a grant for the purchase of this property we shall be doing right ia altering it without the sanction of the Education Department? The CHAIRMAN: As we pay it out of the year's income I do not see that we need to ask permission. Rev. W. FENNELLY There is no depreciation in its value by these arrangements. The CHAIRMAN: I believe it will be worth much more, so that if Father Fennelly wants to buy it in the future he would be prepared to give us more money for it. The resolution was passed unanimously. It was also agreed that Mr. W. E. Lea should be asked to send in a tender for heating the building. EDUCATIONAL RFTUPNS.

Mr. BOWYER presented his monthly. retnrns from the public elementary schools for November, which were as follows :—Certified Government accommodation 2,289, No. on the rolls 2,759, average attendance 1,9771; average attendance for November, 1880, 1,895.3 ; average attend- ance for the year 1874, 1,252; accommodation in excess of average attendance 311.9, number on the rolls in excess of accommodation 470. These figures showed an increaee in the average attendance, as compared with the corresponding period of last year, of 81.8, and an increase, as compared with 1874, the year preceding the formation of the Board, of 7251. The total number in attendance at private adven- ture schools under 9d. per week was 68„ Duringlithe past month he had summoned before magistrates all the cases ordered to be dealt with for contravention of the bye-laws. Convictions were granted in each case, and the usual 59 including costs, imposed.

THE BOAT CHILDREN. The CLERIt read a communication from Mr. Brookes, secretary to the Runcorn Commissioners, in reference to the boat children. It appeared there had been 757 boats registered in Runcorn, with accommodation for 3,107 peso' a above the age of 12 years. In the case of boats built after the 30th June, 1878, three children under the age of 12 years might be reckoned. The Clerk remarked that if they reckoned two children for each boat, it would give 1,500 children to be provided for. The CHAIRMAN : You see what is before us, gentlemen. (Laughter). • Mr, BRISOOE said it appeared from inquiries instituted by the Commissioners that there were not nearly so many

, This Company supplies'a manifest want and effects an evident improvement in Fire Insurance business. Its establishment, moreover, does not increase the number of existing Fire Offices, as it proposes to absorb a going concerm and thus start with a Premium Income exceeding £20,000 per annum. PERPETUAL AND GENERAL. FIRE INSURANCE COMPANY, LIMITED.—Incorporated under the Com- panies' Acts, 1862 to 1880. Capital £1,000,000, in 100,000 lehares of £lO each (of which £3 per Share is to be paid up Within 12 months), entitled out of profits to annual Dividends not exceeding Six per Cent. on the amount called up and paid, and to Forty per Cent, of the Surplus Profits to be divided pro rata every fifth year. First issue-55,000 Shares, payable 10s. on application, 10s. on allotment. 20s. three months after allotment, and 203,. six months after allotment, no further call being contemplated. In the event of no allotment the deposit will be returned in full. Subscribers may pay up their shares in full on allotment, and interest at the rate of £3 per cent, per annum will be allowed on the amount so paid in anticipation until called Up, TRUSTEES OF,TIIE PERPETUAL FIRE INSURANCE FUND. Edward Temperley Gourley, Esq., M.P. Walter N. Molesworth St. Aubyn, Esq., M.P. DIRECTORS. The Hon. 'Mark Pleydell Bouverie (Messrs. Borne, Turner and Co ), 150, Leadenhall-street, E.C. The Hon. Gerald C. Talbot. Director of the National Life Assn- ranze Society, 2, King William-street, E.C. Sir Wilford Brett, K,C.M.G. (Director of the Chelsea Water- works Company, Esher, Surrey. Sir Antonio Brady, J.P. (Director of the Foreign and Colonial Government Trust Company, Limited), Maryland Point, Stratford, Essex. Gordon Kenmure Hardie, Esq.. Ealing, Middlesex. Frederick Perigal, Esq., Thornton Heath, Croydon. NV, L. Williams, Esq. (Messrs. W. Williams and Son, Bread- street, Cheapside, E.O. The Articles of Association provide that two additional Directors shall be elected by the Shareholders at a General Meeting within one month after the first-allotment of Shares. Massey. ABRIDGED PROSPECTUS. This Company is formed to introduce a new method of In- suring Private Dwelling-houses and their contents by means of a Perpetual Insurance Fund, which affords Insurers an advan- tage not offered by any other Company. Approved Private Dwellings will be insured in perpetuity for a single payment of £1 Is. Od. per cent., and the payment of even total Losses will not cancel the policies, which will still remain in full force without further payment by the insured. Perpetual policy contracts purchased for future use or for investment bear interest at the rate of 31 per cent, per annum on the price paid to the Company until applied to the insurance of prOperty, t Perpetual policy holders will be secured by the formation of a Perpetual Insurance Fund, the principal of which will belong to the insured themselves, and be invested in the names of Trustees. This fund will be inalienable for any purposes what- ever. Ilie Scrip of this Perpetual Insurance Fund will be limited to 500,000 cortracts, exchangeable for perpetual policies of £lOO each, and thus, when the whole number is complete, it may fairly be anticipated. having regard to the safe nature of the investment, and the great benefits resulting therefrom, that the policies will be saleable at a considerable premium. Every other description of Fire Insurance will also be trans- - rusted on terms and 'conditions similar to those ad3pted by the leading offices in Great Britain, but on a modified basis which secures a periodical return of 60 per cent, of the surplus profits to the holders of current annual policies. A provisional contract has been entered into for acquiring, on terms favourable to this Company, the business ot an existing Fire Office, with a premium income of upwards of £20,0 0 per annum, which is capable of rapid development. The considera- tion consists entirely of partly paid up shares of this Company. The issue of 500,000 Perpetual Policies will produce a sum of £625,000 which invested in first class securities at 4 per cent., will yield £25,000. From this deduct Fire losses at 6d per cent on 500,000 policies of £lOO each—Sl2,soo, and proportion of expenses of management chargeable to this Branch, say 20 per cent, on the Income—Es,ooo, and there remains a profit balance of £7,000 from the class of business alone; to which will have to be added the large profits that may reasonably be expected from the Company's General Insurance Branch. Detailed Prespectuses, full information and Forms of Appli- cation for shares, may be obtained from the Company's Bankers or Solicitors, and at the offices, No. 11, George Yard, Lombard Street,London, E.C.
